thread:
nina: kicking off monthly least-privilege blitz results review. scanner reported ~243 candidate admin entitlements across projects. dropping summary here for quick triage.

omar: thanks. any high-risk hits (KMS/data/production-admins)?

nina: mostly project-editor and a few cloudkms.admin on legacy projects. sample list: proj-payments: serviceAccount:ingest@proj-payments, proj-ml: user:deploy@redwood, infra-shared: svcacct:terraform@infra. full CSV uploaded: gs://redwood-audit/leastpriv/4100001111-summary.csv

sasha: quick note: last run had false positives because scanner didn't account for role-inheritance via folder policies. we should expect noise.

trent: ran the auto-classifier, ~60 flagged as likely false-positive due to "delegated-editor" pattern. classifier rule shown:```yaml
- pattern: project/*/roles/editor-delegated
  action: mark:fp
```

omar: we need owner ack for any removals. let's avoid mass-removal until owners sign off. can we produce owner contact mapping?

iam-bot: Owner mapping generated. Mapped 243 entitlements to 47 owners. Example: proj-payments -> @billing-eng; proj-ml -> @ml-platform; infra-shared -> @infra-automation. Owner map: /infra/owners/4100001111-owners.json :robot_face:

sasha: here's the gotcha I found: some CI runners rely on project-level editor because they assume cross-project secret access. Before any change we must enumerate runtime paths. grep I used:```bash
# find callers of service account
gcloud logging read 'protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail:serviceAccount:*' --project=proj-payments --format json | jq '.[] | .protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail' | sort -u
```

nina: good. proposal: 3-step flow: 1) mark likely-fp in the ticket and notify owners 2) run a 7-day monitoring window with permission-deny alerting but do not change IAM 3) schedule staged removals for confirmed stale entitlements with rollback scripts.

trent: can we reduce noise by adding an exemption tag for known delegations instead of blanket ignores? maybe a label convention like iam:delegated=true and have scanner treat those as informational.

omar: fine, but we need policy to prevent overuse. Security will require justification notes and review every 90 days.

security-eng: agreed. create a short template for exemption requests: justification, owner, last-rotation, runtime evidence, expiry date. We'll auto-approve 7-day short exemptions for CI migrations.

iam-bot: sample exemption command (to be used by owners):```bash
# add exemption label to resource
gcloud projects update proj-payments --update-labels=iam_delegated=true
```

sasha: audit logs question: current retention for admin-binding changes is 180 days for most projects but not for legacy ones. request a retention increase for projects tagged PG-SENSITIVE via infra ticket.

nina: I'll open INFRA-1428 to extend to 365 days for PG-SENSITIVE. linking ticket in the blitz task.

trent: automation note: the removal playbook will use a canary-first approach: remove binding on single non-prod project, observe 24h, then runhousekeeping across other projects. rollback snippet:```bash
# rebind if rollback needed
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding $PROJECT --member="$MEMBER" --role="$ROLE"
```

omar: alerts: set a short-term detection rule: if permission_denied errors for a service account increase >3% in 1h, trigger page to #eng-oncall and open change rollback.

iam-bot: ran a simulated prune (dry-run) against a sandbox and produced a diff. Summary: 18 removals would affect CI pipelines but no production API keys. Dry-run report: gs://redwood-audit/leastpriv/4100001111-dryrun.json

sasha: can the scanner surface the last-used timestamp per binding? that's the quickest heuristic for staleness.

iam-bot: yes, adding lastUsed to output. example:```json
{"binding":"roles/editor","member":"serviceAccount:terraform@infra","lastUsed":"2025-11-12T03:21:04Z"}
```

nina: next steps (actionable): 1) ticket INFRA-1428 for retention (nina) 2) owners notified with owner map (iam-bot) 3) 7-day monitor flag created for each owner-approved candidate (trent) 4) exemption template live in docs (security-eng). I'll post the checklist in the task and follow up next week.

omar: one last ask: include a small runbook snippet for incident responders on how to quickly rebind keys and where to fetch evidence. example in ticket please.

security-eng: will add runbook steps: evidence path, rebind commands, who to page, and audit export commands.

trent: thanks everyone. closing this triage thread; will update when owners start acking. :white_check_mark:
